title: Multithreading
objectives: Create threads safely and use executors
Apply synchronization and the volatile keyword

sections.markdown: Multithreading runs multiple threads concurrently within one process to use multiple cores and keep apps responsive. Threads share memory, so coordination is required.
Assuming `volatile` makes `count++` thread-safe. It guarantees visibility, not atomicity — read-modify-write still races. Use AtomicInteger or synchronized.
The Java Memory Model defines happens-before: synchronized/volatile/Thread.start ensure one thread's writes are visible to another. Without it, the JVM may reorder or cache values.
Prefer high-level concurrency (ExecutorService, CompletableFuture, concurrent collections) over raw threads and locks. Minimize shared mutable state.

flashcards.back: volatile guarantees visibility only; synchronized guarantees mutual exclusion + visibility.

flashcards.front: Why use a thread pool over new Thread()?
flashcards.back: Reuses threads, bounds concurrency, and avoids the cost of creating/destroying threads per task.
A JMM ordering guarantee ensuring one thread's writes are visible to another (via synchronized/volatile/etc.).

quiz.explain: volatile ensures reads see the latest write but does NOT make compound operations atomic.
AtomicInteger uses CAS for atomic increments without locks.

quiz.q: Preferred way to run many short tasks?
quiz.explain: A pool reuses threads and bounds resource usage.

challenges.text: Run 1000 increments across threads; show the race, then fix with AtomicInteger.
Use CompletableFuture to run two calls in parallel and combine results.
Build a bounded thread pool from scratch with a task queue and worker threads.
